ppr-knowledge-graph.title: Mitigating Undesired Conditions in Flexible Production with Product-Process-Resource Asset Knowledge Graphs (arXiv)
ppr-knowledge-graph.notes: The product-process-resource (PPR) model, which the paper traces to ISA-95 and VDI 3682, describes a production system through three things: the products being made, the processes that make them and the resources that carry those processes out. The paper builds on it to propose a PPR Asset Knowledge Graph, an industry-oriented semantic model implemented as a comprehensive OWL ontology. The aim is to close gaps in conventional model-driven engineering of cyber-physical production systems, especially in representing undesired conditions and errors in flexible production such as robotic workcells, where Industry 4.0 flexibility can undermine classic quality assurance. The graph is paired with large language model chatbots so operators, production planners and engineers can query it in natural language. The authors evaluated it on electric vehicle battery remanufacturing and report that it supports resource allocation based on explicitly modelled capabilities and helps identify and reduce undesired conditions. Caveat: the source is a research abstract and does not mention linking ERP, MES, historian or maintenance records.

csrd.title: Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (Wikipedia)
csrd.notes: The Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive, Directive (EU) 2022/2464, replaces the earlier Non-Financial Reporting Directive and sets a uniform EU framework for reporting non-financial, sustainability information. It was adopted in December 2022, entered into force on 5 January 2023 and applies in stages from 1 January 2024, depending on company size and type. Companies already covered by the old directive were expected to publish first reports in early 2025 for business year 2024. A company is in scope if it exceeds two of three thresholds: 250 employees, a 25 million euro balance sheet or 50 million euro net turnover. This widens coverage to roughly 50,000 organisations in Europe, compared with about 11,600 under the old rules. Unified European reporting standards, developed by EFRAG, are meant to cut disclosure costs and make data comparable for investors. The page notes that national checks mostly stop at confirming data was produced, and that there are no harmonised EU-level control rules or sanctions. It also records the Commission's February 2025 Omnibus proposal and a Stop-the-Clock delay of two years, to 2028, for later waves.

spreadmart.title: Spreadmart (Wikipedia)
spreadmart.notes: A spreadmart, short for spreadsheet data mart, is a business analysis setup built on spreadsheets or other desktop databases that individuals or groups maintain to do work a data mart or data warehouse could do in a more structured way. Because different people build them at different times, with different data sources and different metric definitions, the result is a fragmented, decentralised view of the enterprise. Wayne Eckerson of TDWI coined the term in 2002 as a criticism. Spreadmarts typically arise when standard BI reporting is too slow or inflexible: an analyst exports a table to Excel and builds a private report, copies are emailed around, and the data becomes disconnected from its source so it cannot be verified or refreshed automatically. Undefined, disconnected data can support false conclusions and costly wrong decisions. The page also gives a counter-view by Stephen Samild, who argues that spreadmarts fill roles warehouses cover poorly, such as handling unstructured data, read-write analysis, avoiding long lead times for new sources and free-form presentation. Data marts and data warehouses are the main alternatives.

sparkplug-b.title: IoT Architecture with MQTT Sparkplug B (ISA Interchange)
sparkplug-b.notes: Sparkplug B is a specification that adds industrial conventions on top of MQTT publish/subscribe messaging. It defines a standard topic namespace made of a group ID, an edge node ID, an optional device ID and a message type. The listed message types are NBIRTH and NDEATH for edge nodes, DBIRTH and DDEATH for devices, NDATA and DDATA for data, NCMD and DCMD for commands, and STATE for the host application. Payloads use a compact binary format based on Google Protocol Buffers, which keeps message size and bandwidth low, helpful on WLAN or cellular links, and supports richer data types. A birth certificate describes the device and the data it can send, which lets applications discover sources automatically. A death certificate relies on the MQTT Last Will and Testament mechanism to tell applications a device has gone offline. Data is sent by exception, so only changes are published, and connections are persistent with session awareness. The page says the specification builds on MQTT 3.1.1 and 5.0 and is managed by the Eclipse Foundation within the Eclipse Tahu project.

dispatch-list.title: Manufacturing execution system (Wikipedia)
dispatch-list.notes: This page describes where a dispatch step sits in manufacturing operations. A manufacturing execution system tracks and documents how raw materials become finished goods and watches plant-floor conditions in real time. One of its core functions is dispatching production orders: distributing batches, runs and work orders to work centres and adjusting to unexpected conditions. It sits next to scheduling, which turns production requirements, usually coming from ERP or planning systems, into work orders that make good use of local resources, and next to resource management, which tracks capability and availability. The control systems perform the actual execution while the MES checks resources and reports progress. The page places MES at Level 3 of ISA-95, between ERP at Level 4 and process control at Levels 0 to 2, and says Level 3 activities cover production, quality, logistics and maintenance. Other functions include data collection, performance analysis such as OEE, and track and trace. Caveat: the page does not use the term dispatch list itself.

api-first.title: API-first development (Microsoft)
api-first.notes: API-first development means designing the API contract, meaning endpoints, request and response data and expected errors, before writing the implementation or the user interface. The page treats the API as a product decision because external developers, partners and AI agents will build on it, and contrasts this with code-first, where an API is a by-product of existing code and can leak internal details. The contract is written in a machine-readable format, most often OpenAPI. Once approved, backend teams implement it while front-end and mobile teams build against generated mocks, and documentation, SDKs and tests can be generated from the same source. Versioning is treated as a contract with consumers: additive changes are safe within a version, breaking ones need a new version, and deprecation can be signalled with a Sunset header. One API serves web, mobile, partner and agent clients behind a single gateway, so authentication and rate limiting apply uniformly and business logic is not duplicated. Trade-offs: contract-first adds upfront review, and code-first can suit an early internal tool. The page is a vendor article with Azure-specific content.

nvlink.title: NVLink (Wikipedia)
nvlink.notes: NVLink is Nvidia's wire-based, serial, multi-lane link for short-range data and control transfers between CPUs and GPUs and between GPUs. Unlike PCI Express, one device can have several NVLinks, and devices can form mesh networks instead of depending on a central hub. Nvidia announced it in March 2014; it replaced SLI and uses a proprietary signalling interconnect. The page tabulates generations by theoretical bandwidth: 160 GB/s for version 1.0 (Pascal), 300 GB/s for 2.0 (Volta), 600 GB/s for 3.0 (Ampere), 900 GB/s for 4.0 (Hopper), and 1,800 GB/s for 5.0 (Blackwell), with 6.0 listed at 3.6 TB/s per GPU for Vera Rubin NVL72. Since 2018 NVLink has used NVSwitch, a packet-switched central switch; the Hopper-generation switch can run simple in-network operations such as sum and broadcast. Real-world rates are typically about 90 to 95 percent of the listed maxima. Consumer support was limited and the connector was removed from Ada Lovelace cards in 2022, while datacenter use continues; NVLink Fusion lets chip designers license the technology. Caveat: the page does not mention the GB200 NVL72 rack.

veeam.title: Veeam (Wikipedia)
veeam.notes: Veeam Software Group is a privately held, US-based company, owned by Insight Partners, that develops backup, disaster recovery and data protection software for virtual, cloud-native, SaaS, Kubernetes and physical workloads. It was founded in 2006 by Ratmir Timashev and Andrei Baronov, who had earlier sold Aelita Software to Quest. Its first products handled monitoring and reporting for virtual infrastructure; Veeam Backup & Replication launched in 2008 for VMware vSphere, with Hyper-V support following in 2012. Later products include Veeam Backup for Microsoft Office 365 (2016) and agents for Windows and Linux (2017). The page says it has expanded to protect data on AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Microsoft 365 and Kubernetes. Insight Partners announced a deal of about 5 billion dollars to buy it in January 2020. Acquisitions include Kasten for Kubernetes (2020) and Coveware, a ransomware response firm (April 2024), plus an announced plan in October 2025 to buy Securiti AI for 1.725 billion dollars. Revenue exceeded 1 billion dollars in 2019 and employees numbered about 6,100 in 2025. The page gives conflicting headquarters information.

github-flow.title: GitHub flow (GitHub Docs)
github-flow.notes: GitHub flow is a lightweight, branch-based workflow for collaborating on projects, and GitHub itself uses it for its own policy, documentation and roadmap repositories. The page presents it as useful for anyone working with files in a shared repository, not only developers, and every step can be done in the web interface, with the GitHub CLI or in GitHub Desktop. It has six steps: create a branch with a short descriptive name so the default branch stays untouched; make changes with small, descriptive, isolated commits; open a pull request, optionally as a draft, with a summary and a linked issue; address review comments by pushing more commits; merge once approved, noting that conflicts or branch protection rules such as required approvals can block the merge; and delete the branch to mark the work complete. Deleting the branch does not remove the pull request or its history, and a branch can be restored. The key idea is that changes stay off the default branch until they are reviewed and merged.

isa-95.title: ISA-95 (Wikipedia)
isa-95.notes: ANSI/ISA-95 is an international standard from the International Society of Automation that describes how enterprise systems and control systems should exchange information through an automated interface. It applies to batch, continuous and repetitive manufacturing. Its goals are consistent terminology, information models and operations models shared between suppliers and manufacturers. Part 1 defines terminology and object models, including a hierarchy model based on the Purdue model, equipment hierarchy, functional data-flow models and operations activity models. Part 2 gives the attributes of each object, Part 3 covers manufacturing operations management activities at level 3, the production and MES layer, Part 4 covers objects and attributes for operations management, and Part 5 covers business-to-manufacturing transactions. The reference list also names further parts on messaging, alias services and information exchange profiles. The standard supplies reference models for production, quality, maintenance and inventory activities and the information passed between them. Caveat: the page does not describe the individual levels in detail, mentions only level 3, and notes that its edition dates conflict and that the article may be poorly organised.

now-assist.title: Now Assist (ServiceNow documentation)
now-assist.notes: The documentation page describes Now Assist as ServiceNow's AI assistant, which administrators monitor through the AI Admin Hub, formerly called the Now Assist Admin Console. The hub is used to analyse performance, manage user roles and data usage policies, handle domain separation, and explore, configure and analyse generative AI features and skills. Which Now Assist features, generative AI skills, agentic workflows and AI agents a customer gets depends on the licence tier, and some AI products are unavailable or limited for in-country SKUs, FedRAMP and similar regulated environments, and self-hosted setups. On data handling, the page says customer data moves from individual instances to a central ServiceNow environment that may be in another region and may involve third-party cloud providers, and that inputs, outputs and edits are used to improve AI technologies, with an opt-out for future collection. It warns that AI output may be inaccurate or incomplete and should be validated with human oversight, and that use must follow ServiceNow's AI Acceptable Use Policy. From the Brazil release (29 October 2026) AI Admin Hub is being replaced by AI Admin Center.

product-information-management.title: Product information management (Wikipedia)
product-information-management.notes: Product information management (PIM) is the process of managing all the information needed to market and sell products through distribution channels, with the data created internally to support a multichannel strategy. A PIM acts as a central hub that gathers product data otherwise scattered across departments and formats and distributes it to e-commerce sites, print catalogues, marketplaces such as Amazon and Google Shopping, social media and trading-partner data feeds. Typical functions include centralisation, multi-language and multi-market support, maintenance within a central catalogue, automation of product creation, data governance and output, catalogue grouping for target markets, access control through a web administration interface, and links to ordering and inventory systems. Exchange standards such as Open ICEcat are supported. Technically it runs over or alongside a database and application server and may use XML-based exchange. The page relates PIM to product data management, product lifecycle management, digital asset management and master data management, noting that generic MDM often lacks product-specific enrichment, validation and workflow rules. It is most relevant to B2C and B2B firms selling through several channels.

learning-management-system.title: Learning management system (Wikipedia)
learning-management-system.notes: A learning management system (LMS) is software for administering, documenting, tracking, reporting, automating and delivering courses, training programmes and learning materials. It grew out of e-learning, the first LMS appeared in the late 1990s, and LMSs form the largest segment of the learning systems market. Core functions are hosting content for asynchronous and live learning, course creation in modules, assessments with many question types, tracking and analytics on completion and success, communication tools such as discussion boards, user and role management, and course recommendations based on skill profiles. Deployment can be vendor-hosted (cloud or SaaS) or locally hosted, often with open-source software. Content integration relies on standards such as AICC, SCORM, xAPI and LTI, though the page notes SCORM is not always necessary and can be restrictive. As of 2023 the leading US higher-education systems were Canvas, D2L Brightspace, Blackboard Learn and Moodle. The page lists interoperability, accessibility, reusability and maintainability as advantages, and warns that simply moving face-to-face material online can produce low interactivity. Research results on LMS effectiveness are mixed.

meta-quest.title: Meta Quest (Wikipedia)
meta-quest.notes: Meta Quest, called Oculus Quest until August 2022, is a line of virtual reality headsets with augmented reality capabilities developed by Reality Labs, a Meta division. The first Oculus Quest shipped on 21 May 2019, and over 20 million Quest headsets had been sold by February 2023. The headsets run an Android-based operating system, now Horizon OS, work standalone and wirelessly, track in six degrees of freedom with built-in cameras rather than external sensors, support hand tracking, and can connect to a PC for Rift-compatible software. Passthrough lets users see the room, and colour passthrough arrived with the Quest Pro. The page lists models: Oculus Quest (2019), Quest 2 (October 2020), Meta Quest Pro (October 2022, 1,499.99 US dollars at launch, with eye and face tracking cameras and Touch Pro controllers), Meta Quest 3 (October 2023, 499 or 649 dollars, Snapdragon XR2 Gen 2, 8 GB RAM, 2064 by 2208 pixels per eye, 515 g) and Quest 3S (October 2024). Quest 3 and 3S were still sold; Quest 2 and Pro were discontinued in September 2024.

mfa-fatigue.title: Multi-factor authentication (Wikipedia)
mfa-fatigue.notes: The page's MFA article describes MFA fatigue, which it also calls MFA bombing, as an increasingly common way to defeat multi-factor authentication. Where an authenticator app sends push notifications, an attacker who is already trying to log in can trigger a flood of approval requests, hoping the user eventually accepts one by mistake, out of annoyance or confusion. The attack may be combined with social engineering, such as calls pretending to be IT support. The page names a September 2022 breach of Uber by a Lapsus$ member as an example and mentions a claimed 2024 case involving Apple customers, which is marked as needing a citation. As a mitigation, the page says that in 2022 Microsoft added an option to its Authenticator app that requires the user to type a number in addition to tapping approve. It does not say how well this works. Caveat: the page does not use the terms push bombing or prompt bombing, and it treats the topic as one section of a broader article rather than a dedicated page.

trunk-based-development.title: Trunk Based Development
trunk-based-development.notes: Trunk-based development is a source-control branching model in which developers collaborate on a single branch, the trunk, which in Git is usually main. Teams avoid long-lived development branches and use documented techniques instead, which the site says prevents merge problems and broken builds. Small teams may commit straight to trunk; larger teams use pull requests, but the feature branches must be short-lived and come from one developer workstation. Short-lived branches exist for code review and CI checks, not for building or publishing artifacts. Release branches, if used, are cut from trunk just in time, hardened and deleted, or teams release from trunk and fix forward. Key practices include a full pre-integration build on the workstation, committing to trunk at least once every 24 hours, a build server that confirms commits do not break the build, branch by abstraction for larger changes, feature flags, eager code review and keeping the codebase releasable on demand. The model enables continuous integration and continuous delivery. The site says Google practises it with a monorepo and reportedly about 35,000 developers, and compares GitHub Flow as similar but differing in where releases come from.

nvidia-blackwell.title: Blackwell (microarchitecture) (Wikipedia)
nvidia-blackwell.notes: Blackwell is an Nvidia GPU microarchitecture that succeeds Hopper in the datacenter and Ada Lovelace in consumer products, named after statistician David Blackwell, with Rubin as its successor. It was officially announced at GTC on 18 March 2024, centred on the B100 and B200, the eight-GPU HGX B200 board and the 72-GPU NVL72 rack. Datacenter parts use TSMC 4NP; the GB100 die has 104 billion transistors, and the B100 package joins two dies through a 10 TB/s link into one cache-coherent chip of 208 billion transistors, using HBM3E memory and PCIe 6.0. The B200 SXM variant has 192 GB of memory. New features include fifth-generation Tensor Cores with native low-precision formats such as MXFP6 and MXFP4, a second-generation Transformer Engine, with Nvidia claiming 20 petaflops of FP4 compute for the GB200 superchip, fourth-generation RT cores and a RISC-V AI Management Processor. Consumer parts use GDDR7 and PCIe 5.0, led by the RTX 5090 with 24,576 CUDA cores. The page also notes a design flaw reported in October 2024 that lowered yields, and says 2025 production was reported as sold out.

flow-efficiency.title: Flow efficiency (Scrum.org article)
flow-efficiency.notes: Flow efficiency is the share of a work item's total elapsed time during which someone is actively working on it, with the rest being waiting. The article gives the formula as active time divided by total time, times 100, and presents it as a diagnostic for latency rather than a target. In its worked example, a feature that takes 20 days end to end but needs only 4 days of active work has a flow efficiency of 20 percent, meaning 16 days of waiting. The article claims most product teams sit at roughly 15 to 25 percent, which it describes as three to five hours of waiting per hour of work. It contrasts the metric with velocity and throughput, which show how much is delivered but not why it is slow, and places it among five flow metrics attributed to Mik Kersten: flow time, flow velocity, flow efficiency, flow load and flow distribution. It names common bottlenecks such as handoffs between teams, approval chains, context switching from too much work in progress, technical debt and slow decisions, and suggests a four-week diagnostic. Some business claims it cites are attributed to outside research and are not verified.

hardware-root-of-trust.title: Microsoft Pluton security processor (Microsoft Learn)
hardware-root-of-trust.notes: This Microsoft Learn page describes a concrete hardware root of trust, Microsoft Pluton, a chip-to-cloud security technology that provides a hardware-based root of trust, secure identity, secure attestation and cryptographic services. Pluton combines a secure subsystem built into the CPU's system-on-chip with Microsoft-authored software. It protects credentials, identities, personal data and encryption keys, which the page says are significantly harder to remove even if an attacker installs malware or has full physical access to the PC. It can provide TPM functionality and go beyond the TPM 2.0 specification. The root of trust matters because a TPM keeps a tamper-resistant log of system state that services can cryptographically verify, so malware on the device cannot feed false health signals to services such as Intune. Pluton has three layers: a secure element in the SoC giving a trusted execution environment, Microsoft firmware loaded at boot and updatable through Windows Update, and OS drivers and software. It builds on technology from Xbox and Azure Sphere, is supported on certain AMD, Intel and Qualcomm chips, and its firmware is planned to use a Rust foundation for memory safety.

constraint-based-scheduling.title: Advanced planning and scheduling (Wikipedia)
constraint-based-scheduling.notes: The page on advanced planning and scheduling (APS) covers the planning approach that constraint-based scheduling belongs to. APS is a manufacturing management process that allocates raw materials and production capacity as optimally as possible to meet demand, and suits environments where simpler planning methods cannot handle complex trade-offs between competing priorities. Because the solution space grows roughly factorially with the number of products, production scheduling is inherently very hard. The page criticises traditional systems such as manufacturing resource planning, which allocate materials and capacity stepwise and separately, often ignore constraints and can therefore produce infeasible plans that adapt poorly to changes in demand, capacity or material availability. APS instead plans and schedules simultaneously based on available materials, labour and plant capacity. It is commonly used in make-to-order manufacturing, capital-intensive processes with constrained plant capacity, plants where many products compete for the same capacity, products with many components or tasks, and production needing frequent unpredictable schedule changes. Caveat: the page does not use the phrase constraint-based scheduling and does not discuss specific constraint types or solvers.

freelancing.title: Freelancer (Wikipedia)
freelancing.notes: A freelancer is a self-employed person who is not tied long-term to a single employer, and the page notes that legal and financial contexts usually say independent contractor. Freelancing is especially common in music, writing, acting, programming, web and graphic design, translation, illustration and film production. Freelancers may work through agencies or find clients themselves, and they handle contracts, accounting and marketing on their own. Rates may be hourly, daily, per piece, per project or value-based, with payment upfront, on completion or by milestones, and payment is never guaranteed. Cited benefits are flexibility and the ability to choose clients; drawbacks are the lack of pensions, sick pay, paid holidays and employer health insurance, late payments and gaps between jobs. The page covers legal issues such as misclassification of employees as contractors, UK IR35 rules and copyright, where the author owns work by default unless a contract states work for hire. It notes the EU has no legal definition of freelancer. Statistics are mostly Western, for example about 10.3 million US independent contractors in 2005 and an estimated 162 million independent workers in Europe and the US in 2018.

strategy-pattern.title: Strategy pattern (Wikipedia)
strategy-pattern.notes: The strategy pattern, also called the policy pattern, is a behavioural design pattern from the Gang of Four book that lets a program choose an algorithm at runtime. Instead of hard-coding one algorithm, calling code receives instructions about which member of a family of algorithms to use, so the algorithm can vary independently from the clients that use it. In the UML structure, a context object does not implement the algorithm itself but refers to a strategy interface and calls its method; concrete strategy classes implement that interface, and the context can switch from one to another while running. The pattern can be realised with function pointers, first-class functions, classes or reflection. A typical use is a validation class that selects a validation algorithm depending on the data type, source or user choice, with the algorithms kept separate so other objects can reuse them. The page links the pattern to composition over inheritance, the open-closed principle and decoupling. Its car example puts braking behaviour behind an interface with simple and anti-lock implementations, so a car's braking can be replaced without subclass duplication.

minecraft.title: Minecraft (Wikipedia)
minecraft.notes: Minecraft is a 3D sandbox video game developed and published by Mojang Studios, created originally by Markus Persson in Java, with Jens Bergensten leading development after the full release in November 2011. Microsoft bought Mojang and the Minecraft rights for 2.5 billion US dollars, announced on 15 September 2014. Xbox Game Studios publishes the cross-platform Bedrock Edition, while Java Edition stays PC-only. Gameplay modes include Survival, Hardcore with permadeath, Creative with unlimited resources and flying, and Adventure, plus multiplayer through servers, LAN, split screen and Realms. The public alpha began on 17 May 2009 and the full PC release followed on 18 November 2011. The page reports more than 400 million copies sold as of May 2026, making it the best-selling video game of all time. On education, MinecraftEdu began in 2011 and Minecraft: Education Edition launched on 1 November 2016 with lesson plans for up to 30 students; teachers use it for history, language arts and science, and Microsoft and Code.org reported over 85 million children had used their Minecraft-based coding resources by 2018.

marketing-manager.title: Marketing management (Wikipedia)
marketing-manager.notes: This page covers marketing management, the discipline behind the marketing manager role. It defines it as applying marketing orientation, techniques and methods within organisations and managing marketing resources and activities, and quotes Kotler's framing as the analysis, planning, implementation and control of programmes meant to produce exchanges with target audiences. Managers analyse the industry and competitors with tools such as Porter's five forces and SWOT, run market research that can be qualitative, quantitative, experimental or observational, and carry out brand audits. They choose attractive target segments, define a brand's positioning around a differentiated key benefit, and set strategy through the marketing mix of product, price, place and promotion. A marketing plan typically has an executive summary, situation analysis, objectives, chosen strategy and segments, and implementation for each of the four Ps. Managers also improve core processes such as new product development, brand management and pricing, manage vendors such as agencies, and track progress with metrics, forecasts and CRM tools. The role varies with company size: in small firms it blends management and hands-on work, in large consumer firms it can resemble a general manager for one product.

openrewrite.title: OpenRewrite documentation
openrewrite.notes: OpenRewrite is an open-source ecosystem for automated source-code refactoring whose stated goal is to help developers eliminate technical debt in their repositories. It runs prepackaged, open-source recipes for framework migrations, security fixes and stylistic consistency, aiming to cut effort from hours or days to minutes. It was originally Java-focused, and the community is widening language and framework coverage. Recipes are the units users run and are built from visitors, which make the actual modifications; the page's example is a visitor that turns assertTrue calls into static imports consistently across test files. Technically, OpenRewrite modifies Lossless Semantic Trees that represent the source code and then prints the changed trees back as source, so changes are minimally invasive and preserve original formatting, letting people review a diff and commit. Gradle and Maven plugins run recipes on one repository at a time, while Moderne is the commercial platform for running the recipe catalogue across many repositories with mass commits and impact analysis, with a free public service for open-source projects and a multi-repo CLI. The page notes recipes are moving from Maven Central to the Code Genome Project.

higgsfield.title: Higgsfield AI (Wikipedia)
higgsfield.notes: Higgsfield AI is a private generative AI company based in San Francisco that builds software for creating and editing video and images. It is best known for a workflow-oriented platform used by creators and marketing teams to make short-form social content and advertising material. The product combines several AI models and editing tools into guided creation flows, integrates third-party models, and, according to Reuters, uses an internal reasoning engine meant to improve consistency in generated video. A browser-based end-to-end video creation tool launched in March 2025, and OpenAI cited the company as an application using its models for planning and video generation. The company was founded in 2023 by Alex Mashrabov, who previously led generative AI at Snap, and Erzat Dulat, and has ties to Kazakhstan through the Astana Hub programme. TechCrunch covered its April 2024 launch as a challenger to OpenAI's Sora. In January 2026 it announced an 80 million dollar extension to its Series A at a valuation above 1.3 billion dollars, with reports giving a total Series A of 130 million. Caveat: the page does not describe camera presets, motion control or lip sync tools.

service-catalog.title: Service catalog (Wikipedia)
service-catalog.notes: A service catalog is a curated collection of business and IT services within an enterprise, implemented in software as a digital registry that also works as a knowledge management tool. Services are typically repeatable, with controlled inputs, outputs and procedures. Each entry usually has a named accountable owner, a name or identifier, a description, a category, related request types and supporting services, who may request or view it, any costs, how it is requested and fulfilled, and escalation points and key contacts. The catalogue centralises services so distributed organisations use the same ones instead of duplicate local versions, reveals gaps and redundancies, shows which people and systems are allocated to each service, and tracks demand metrics such as most and least used services, approval and delivery times and spending. Users search or browse by category, review details, submit a request and follow its status. Under ITIL, an IT service catalogue is the published part of the service portfolio, and cloud service catalogues work as self-service portals with standardised definitions. Caveat: the page frames the concept around business and IT services and requests, not specifically a developer catalogue of software components.

ralph-loop.title: Ralph Wiggum as a software engineer (Geoffrey Huntley)
ralph-loop.notes: This is the original write-up of the Ralph technique, named after the Simpsons character. In its purest form it is a Bash loop that repeatedly feeds the same prompt file to a coding agent, so the agent keeps working instead of stopping. The author says it works with any tool that does not cap tool calls and usage. Ralph is monolithic: one process in one repository doing one item per loop, choosing the most important task from a plan file. Each loop reloads the same stable inputs, the plan and the specifications, to keep context consistent, and the main context acts as a scheduler while subagents do expensive searching and summarising. Quality comes from backpressure such as type systems, tests and static analysers that reject bad output, and the operator tunes the prompt with explicit instructions when Ralph misbehaves, for example forbidding placeholder implementations. The author reports building a programming language with it and a contract delivered for 297 dollars in API costs. Caveats stated on the page: output is nondeterministic, the code may not compile, senior engineering judgement is still needed, he would not use it on an existing codebase, and repeated loops consume many tokens.

github-copilot-sdk.title: github/copilot-sdk (GitHub repository)
github-copilot-sdk.notes: The repository describes the GitHub Copilot SDK as a multi-platform SDK for embedding the Copilot agent in apps and services. It exposes the same engine as the Copilot CLI as a programmable agent runtime: developers define agent behaviour while Copilot handles planning, tool calls and file edits. SDKs exist for Node.js and TypeScript, Python, Go, .NET, Rust and Java. Each client talks to the Copilot CLI running in server mode over JSON-RPC and manages that process automatically; the CLI is bundled for Node.js, Python and .NET but must be installed for Go, Java and Rust. Developers can define custom agents, skills and tools, and by default the first-party CLI tools are exposed with a permission handler governing each call. All models available through the CLI are supported. A Copilot subscription is required unless bring-your-own-key is used, which supports providers such as OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry and Anthropic with key-based authentication only. The page calls the SDK generally available under semantic versioning, licensed under MIT, and says it is being renamed Microsoft Copilot SDK with the repository moving to the Microsoft organisation in phases. It does not describe MCP integration in detail.

aws-iam.title: What is IAM? (AWS IAM User Guide)
aws-iam.notes: AWS Identity and Access Management is a web service for securely controlling access to AWS resources. It covers authentication, verifying who is signing in, and authorisation, deciding what an authenticated identity may do, across AWS accounts. Every account starts with a root user that has full access to everything, and AWS strongly recommends not using it for daily tasks but creating other identities such as administrators, analysts and developers with only the access they need. Access works in steps: a user signs in and is matched to a trusted principal, which can be an IAM user, a federated principal from AWS STS, an IAM role or an application; a request then asks for access to a resource, and AWS checks the identity and the policies that enforce the access level; once authorised, the principal can act, for example launching an EC2 instance or deleting S3 buckets. Requests can come from the same account or a trusted other account. IAM is eventually consistent, so changes take time to replicate and should not sit in critical code paths. IAM, IAM Identity Center and STS are free; users pay only for the other services they use, and some IAM Access Analyzer checks carry charges.

work-in-progress.title: Work in process (Wikipedia)
work-in-progress.notes: Work in process, also called work in progress or in-process inventory, is a company's partially finished goods that await completion and sale; the term can also mean the value of those items. It is used in supply chain management and is a key input for inventory on the balance sheet, where it is grouped with raw materials and finished goods under current assets. The page gives the end-of-period calculation as beginning WIP inventory plus production costs minus finished goods, where production costs include raw materials, labour and overhead. In lean thinking, excessive processing of goods or WIP counts as one of the seven wastes because it adds no value. On managing it, the page says low WIP levels are generally ideal and efficient inventory management lowers costs, and that higher WIP can absorb demand surges and shorten cycle time but also raises storage costs, obsolescence risk and waste if demand falls short. Coordination across internal functions and with suppliers and customers is needed, and demand forecasting software can help hold enough WIP without excess stock. It also notes that HMRC has no specific definition and distinguishes manufactured products, service contracts and construction contracts.

dora-metrics.title: DORA's software delivery metrics (dora.dev)
dora-metrics.notes: This DORA guide describes the software delivery performance metrics from the DevOps Research and Assessment programme, run by Google Cloud. It notes the model has moved from the original four keys to five metrics. Throughput metrics are change lead time, the time from commit to production, deployment frequency, and failed deployment recovery time, which replaced the older mean time to restore. Instability metrics are change fail rate, the share of deployments needing immediate intervention such as a rollback or hotfix, and deployment rework rate, the share of unplanned deployments caused by production incidents. DORA's research links these metrics to better organisational performance and team well-being, and the page says speed and stability are not trade-offs because the metrics generally correlate. Guidance includes applying them to one application or service at a time, not comparing very different applications, not turning them into targets because that invites gaming, using several metrics together, sharing ownership across development, operations and release teams, and reducing batch size as a common way to improve all five. The page gives no numeric tier thresholds.

selection-pane.title: Use the Selection Pane to manage objects in documents (Microsoft Support)
selection-pane.notes: The Selection Pane lists the objects in a Word, PowerPoint or Excel document by name so users can reorder them, show or hide them, lock them, rename them, and group or ungroup them. Objects appear in insertion order, and for overlapping objects the top object is at the top of the list. In Word and PowerPoint it opens from Home, Editing, Select, Selection Pane, and in Excel from Find and Select; Alt+F10 also opens it. To reorder, select one or more items and drag them or use Bring Forward and Send Backward; an object inside a group can only move within that group. Grouping uses Ctrl+click and the Group command on the Shape Format tab. Hidden objects stay in the file but are invisible, and Microsoft warns they are easy to forget, while a tip suggests temporarily hiding a top object to edit one beneath it. Renaming works by selecting an item twice or pressing F2, and locking prevents editing. In Word, inline objects appear in the pane but cannot be reordered, hidden or multi-selected. The page lists keyboard shortcuts and covers Microsoft 365 and Office 2016 through 2024, including Mac.

intelligent-recap.title: Intelligent recap for calls and meetings in Teams (Microsoft Learn)
intelligent-recap.notes: Intelligent recap uses AI to reduce note-taking and follow-up for Teams meetings, events and calls. After a meeting, the Recap tab offers AI notes and recommended tasks, personalised timeline markers for mentions, screen shares and joins, speaker markers, chapters and topics, an audio recap and a video recap. Events give recap only to organisers, co-organisers and presenters. For PSTN and peer-to-peer VoIP calls, a Recap button offers AI notes and tasks. It requires a Microsoft 365 subscription with Teams plus a Teams Premium or Microsoft Copilot licence, and the audio recap requires Copilot; PSTN calls also need Teams Phone and a calling plan. Transcription must be enabled, and recording is needed for the full experience, otherwise recap lacks recording, speakers, topics and chapters. Video recap needs a meeting of at least 10 minutes that is recorded and transcribed, and holds up to 100 highlights. Audio recap, in public preview, combines up to eight scheduled meetings and is stored for 60 days. Multilingual recap in public preview translates recaps into participants' languages. Recaps can be shared with external attendees through Outlook.

google-sheets.title: Google Sheets (Wikipedia)
google-sheets.notes: Google Sheets is a web-based spreadsheet program in Google's free Docs Editors suite, also available as Android and iOS apps and a ChromeOS desktop app, and part of Google Workspace. It began as XL2Web from 2Web Technologies, which Google acquired in 2006; it launched as Google Labs Spreadsheets in June 2006 and was renamed Google Sheets in October 2012. Its main strength is real-time collaboration, where several users edit the same file with coloured cursors and a chat sidebar, backed by automatic saving, a revision history with restore, a permissions system and tagging. Explore uses machine learning to answer questions about data, and Gemini was integrated in late 2025 for formulas, charts and summaries. Add-ons extend it, and offline editing works in Chromium browsers via an extension and natively in mobile apps. For Excel compatibility it can view, convert and export formats including xls, xlsx, xlsm, csv, tsv and ods, though it handles the 1900 leap year bug differently from Excel. Documents are capped at 10 million cells. It is free for individuals and included in paid Workspace plans. Password managers warn that Sheets lacks end-to-end encryption.

unified-namespace.title: Elements of the Unified Namespace (HiveMQ)
unified-namespace.notes: HiveMQ describes a unified namespace (UNS) as the real-time, event-driven backbone of an organisation's data architecture, a single source of truth connecting operational technology, IT and business systems. The page argues it is more than an MQTT broker or data pipeline: it must support high-throughput messaging, fine-grained access control, edge and cloud interoperability and historical data integration. MQTT is presented as the best-suited protocol, and the broker is one component of the UNS. Events are published once when generated and made available instantly to many subscribers, which decouples producers from consumers, and subscribers choose topics, using wildcards and filtering to limit traffic. The topic hierarchy should mirror the organisation, such as sites, lines, processes and assets, so data can be found by navigation and sprawl is avoided. Further requirements include scaling, schema registries that enforce data contracts and add context such as units, topic-level access control with TLS, persistence through time-series databases and retained messages, and a hybrid edge and cloud design. Limits: a UNS is built for real-time exchange, so history needs separate persistence, and without data modelling it can become a chaotic message hub. The page is vendor content.

vlan.title: VLAN (Wikipedia)
vlan.notes: A virtual local area network (VLAN) is a broadcast domain at the data link layer that is partitioned and isolated within a network, behaving like a virtual switch that shares physical infrastructure with other VLANs while staying logically separate. Membership is configured in software, so hosts can be grouped even when they are not on the same switch. Frames are identified by an IEEE 802.1Q tag inserted into the Ethernet frame, and a trunk is a link that carries several VLANs. Switches normally do not bridge traffic between VLANs, because that would break the broadcast domain, so a Layer 3 router is needed for traffic that crosses VLANs, and the router filters broadcasts. Common uses are segmenting voice over IP, management, storage networks, guest access and DMZs, isolating hosting customers, reducing broadcast traffic and decoupling users' network location from physical location; VLANs often map one to one to IP subnets. 802.1Q supports up to 4,094 VLANs, with 802.1ad and 802.1aq extending this. Limits include VLAN hopping if switchports are misconfigured, complications with overlapping address ranges and the fact that assignments are not visible in the wiring closet. W. David Sincoskie at Bellcore invented VLAN tagging in the 1980s.

bsi.title: Federal Office for Information Security (Wikipedia)
bsi.notes: The Bundesamt fuer Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik (BSI) is an upper-level federal agency of Germany for information security, founded in 1991 and headquartered in Bonn, with about 1,700 employees in 2024. It reports to the Federal Ministry of the Interior and is led by Claudia Plattner since July 2023. Its scope is set by the BSI Act and covers computer application security, critical infrastructure protection, internet security, cryptography, product certification and accreditation of security test labs. Core tasks include protecting federal networks, testing and certifying IT products, warning about malware and vulnerabilities, consulting the federal administration, raising public awareness, developing binding IT security standards and cryptographic systems. It is Germany's central IT security certification body and references IT-Grundschutz, ITSEC and the Common Criteria; IT-Grundschutz is a set of enterprise security guidelines exceeding 4,800 pages that underlies a certification. Programmes include the National Cyber Defence Centre and the Alliance for Cyber Security, which had more than 6,800 members in 2023. The page says a 2025 law implementing the EU NIS2 directive requires attack reports to the BSI within 24 hours and gives it supervisory powers including fines.

sap-ecc.title: SAP ERP (Wikipedia)
sap-ecc.notes: SAP ERP is enterprise resource planning software from SAP SE covering a company's core business functions, first released in 1972 according to the infobox. The page calls it legacy technology that has been superseded by SAP S/4HANA. It grew from SAP R/3, launched on 6 July 1992. In 2004 SAP ERP was introduced, replacing R/3 Enterprise with the ERP Central Component, SAP ECC, which merged SAP Business Warehouse, Strategic Enterprise Management and the Internet Transaction Server into one instance. SAP ERP 6.0 followed in 2006, and since then new functions have been delivered through optional enhancement packages, the last being EhP8 in 2016, which the page says concludes ECC 6.0's evolution and became the foundation for the move to S/4HANA. Modules include Financial Accounting, Controlling, Sales and Distribution, Materials Management, Production Planning, Quality Management, Plant Maintenance and Human Resources. Traditional implementations have five phases from preparation to go-live support, and the page cites unattributed cost estimates of over 100 million dollars for Fortune 500 projects. Caveat: it gives no standard maintenance end date for ECC; its only dates are 2031 to 2033 for a private-edition transition option.

vat-in-the-digital-age.title: VAT in the Digital Age (Wikipedia)
vat-in-the-digital-age.notes: ViDA is a European Commission package, proposed on 8 December 2022, to modernise the EU VAT system and reduce the VAT gap, which the page cites at 99 billion euros of lost revenue in 2020. The Commission projected up to 18 billion euros of extra annual VAT revenue and about 5 billion euros in yearly compliance savings. It has three pillars, each a legal act adopted on 11 March 2025 and published on 25 March 2025: real-time digital reporting based on e-invoicing (Directive 2025/516), platform economy rules (Regulation 2025/517) and single VAT registration (Implementing Regulation 2025/518). Since April 2025 member states may mandate domestic e-invoicing without a derogation. From 1 July 2030 VAT-registered businesses must issue structured e-invoices for cross-border B2B and B2G supplies, with a harmonised real-time system planned for 1 January 2035. From 1 July 2028 platforms for short-term accommodation and passenger road transport are treated as the deemed supplier, though states may postpone to 2030. The One Stop Shop extends to more B2C supplies starting 1 January 2027, finishing 1 July 2028. Adoption needed unanimity, and Estonia's resistance delayed agreement for about two years.

sap-fiori.title: Introducing SAP Fiori (SAP Learning)
sap-fiori.notes: SAP Learning describes SAP Fiori as the user experience for SAP software and the design language for enterprise applications. SAP introduced Fiori 3 in 2019 to give all SAP products one consistent design. Fiori replaces dense, transaction-centric screens with role-based, task-focused apps for frequent tasks such as approvals, lookups and self-service, for example an Approve Purchase Orders app that shows approvers the key information quickly. Its guidelines include a 5-1-2 principle: five interactions to reach important tasks, one primary action per screen and feedback within two seconds. The design principles are role-based, adaptive across desktop, tablet and phone, coherent, simple and delightful. The SAP Fiori Launchpad is the role-based, personalised entry point, showing app tiles according to roles defined in the SAP system plus a search and explore bar. The technology stack includes SAPUI5, a JavaScript, CSS and HTML5 framework, the Fiori front-end server for the ABAP platform, SAP Gateway with the OData protocol, SAP Business Application Studio for development and SAP Analytics. Clients are any HTML5 browser, SAP Business Client and SAP Mobile Start.

mistral-ocr.title: Document AI OCR processor (Mistral documentation)
mistral-ocr.notes: Mistral's Document AI OCR processor extracts text and structured content from PDFs and images, with the mistral-ocr-latest alias pointing to the newest OCR model. It preserves document structure and hierarchy and returns the result as a JSON object with pages, each containing Markdown, images, tables, hyperlinks, header, footer, dimensions, confidence scores and blocks, plus model and usage information. Tables can be left inline in the Markdown or returned separately as Markdown or HTML tables through the table format parameter, and headers and footers can be extracted separately. Block extraction returns paragraph-level bounding boxes with structural labels such as title, list, table, equation, caption, code and signature, in reading order. Confidence scores are available at page, block or word level, and more than 40 languages are supported. Inputs can be images such as PNG, JPEG and AVIF, or documents such as PDF, PPTX and DOCX, passed as a public URL, Base64 or an uploaded file. Table formatting and header or footer extraction need OCR version 2512 or newer, and block extraction needs OCR 4 or newer. For large volumes Mistral recommends its Batch Inference service, and for structured output, Document Annotations. The page does not mention Azure AI Foundry.

seedance.title: Seedance (Wikipedia)
seedance.notes: Seedance is a text-to-video AI model developed by ByteDance and first released in June 2025. Seedance 2.0 followed in February 2026 and went viral for realistic clips, such as celebrity fight scenes and cartoon characters rendered as otters, and Seedance 2.5, dated July 2026, is listed as the current stable release. The page says Seedance 2.5 generates native videos up to 30 seconds, accepts up to 50 multimodal references, supports local editing so a single detail such as hair colour can change without regenerating the clip and keeps approved performances, expressions and lighting, and includes a beta long-video mode extending clips to three minutes. The page also records controversy: the Motion Picture Association condemned it for copyright infringement, Disney sent ByteDance a cease-and-desist letter in February 2026 and Paramount Skydance made similar accusations, ByteDance said on 16 February 2026 it would strengthen safeguards, and two US senators urged ByteDance in March 2026 to shut it down. Some commentators questioned whether viral clips were purely AI-generated. Reaction in China was generally enthusiastic. Caveat: the page does not describe the reference inputs of version 2.0.

virtual-desktop-infrastructure.title: Desktop virtualization (Wikipedia)
virtual-desktop-infrastructure.notes: Desktop virtualization separates the desktop environment and its applications from the physical device used to access them. In the remote model, applications run on a remote operating system and only display, keyboard and mouse data travel over the network through a remote display protocol, while data stays on the remote system; clients can be PCs, thin clients, tablets or phones. Virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) is the most common form: several desktop OS instances run as virtual machines on a server under a hypervisor, and the page warns that VDI is often misused to mean any desktop virtualization. VDI gives each user an individual desktop OS and can preserve personal workspaces, whereas remote desktop sessions share one server OS and use far fewer resources, and VDI licensing costs more and is less flexible. Supporting technologies include application virtualization, user virtualization that separates personal settings from the OS, and desktop layering. Cloud options are managed VDI and desktop as a service. Cited benefits are centralised management, easier disaster recovery, improved security because no data is stored on user devices, and running Windows apps on non-Windows devices. The page does not discuss profile loading or storage performance.
